report.summary: Git worktrees share a single object store and index, leading to lock contention on index.lock and race conditions on pack files. At 10 concurrent worktrees, occasional index lock failures are likely; at 100, frequent lock timeouts, operation failures, and possible object store corruption (e.g., concurrent gc) become common. Formal benchmarks are sparse; practitioner reports and mailing list discussions indicate issues beyond ~30-50 worktrees. risks: Windows file locking (antivirus, OS) may worsen contention and cause spurious failures.
Shared object store writes (e.g., `git gc`, `git repack`) can corrupt the database if not serialized.
Many short-lived worktrees increase inode usage and disk churn.
Serializing all Git writes through a single point becomes a bottleneck, limiting true parallelism.
Alternatives like per-agent clones consume more disk space and take longer to initialize.
todos: Implement a write-serializing adapter around Git operations (e.g., a queue or lock file) to avoid index/store contention among worktrees.
Benchmark the system at 10 and 100 simulated parallel agents, measuring lock contention rate, operation latency, and failure frequency.
Evaluate per-agent thin clones (e.g., `git clone --shared` from a bare reference repo) as a fallback; compare disk and time overhead.
Ensure no automatic garbage collection on shared object stores and add health checks for repository corruption.
If adopting worktrees, add retry logic with exponential backoff for index lock errors.

handoff.suggestion: Start with a small pilot: run 10 agents with worktrees and monitor lock errors. Then spike 100 agents using a file-based job queue for Git writes. If contention is unmanageable, prototype per-agent clones seeded from a common bare repository (read-only) and measure the trade-offs. Also investigate Git's `core.fscache` and `core.preloadindex` on Windows to mitigate some performance issues. For deeper background, review Git mailing list threads on 'worktree scalability' and the Git for Windows issues tracker.

name: q31-worktree-parallel-agents
question: Git worktree strategies for many parallel agents: what breaks at ten and at a hundred concurrent worktrees, how do teams handle shared object-store contention and index locks, and what is the practical alternative when worktrees stop scaling?
